maturity_scale.2: Ad hoc, happens but isn't documented or consistent
maturity_scale.3: Defined, a process exists but isn't consistently followed
maturity_scale.5: Fully embedded, routine, monitored, and improved over time

questions.text: Does a register of AI systems in use across the organisation exist at all?
Does each register entry capture a named owner (a role, not an individual), purpose, deployment status, and data sources, in line with ATRS's own field structure?
Is a risk tier recorded against each system on the register, distinct from a general sense of how risky it feels?
Are high-risk systems reviewed at least every six months against a defined schedule, rather than whenever someone remembers to check?
Are decommissioned systems kept on the register with their downstream dependencies documented, rather than deleted once retired?
Is there a defined process for classifying each AI system into a risk tier before it is deployed, not after?
Does that process explicitly check the system against the EU AI Act's prohibited practices before considering anything else?
For systems touching patient care, is a severity and likelihood clinical risk matrix applied and recorded in a Clinical Safety Case Report?
Is risk classification reassessed on defined triggers, a change of purpose, a new data source, rather than treated as a one-time label?
Is there a named, senior role, separate from the system owner, who confirms and signs off each risk tier before deployment?
Is a Data Protection Impact Assessment completed before build begins for any system meeting UK GDPR's high-risk processing triggers?
Does the assessment separately identify allocative harm (unfair distribution of opportunity) and representational harm (reinforced stereotyping), rather than one generic bias line?
Is residual risk explicitly recorded, with a documented process for escalating to the ICO where it cannot be sufficiently reduced?
For health systems, is a DTAC assessment completed with each of its five domains signed off by its own named accountable officer?
Is the impact assessment revisited on the same triggers as the risk tier, rather than treated as a one-time gate at launch?
Is bias testing performed against all nine protected characteristics before deployment, not just the ones that seem obviously relevant?
Does bias testing account for proxy variables, rather than relying on removing protected characteristics from the training data?
Where a disparity is found, is a documented, evidenced proportionality case made, rather than an assertion that the model is accurate?
For public sector deployments, is a Section 149 public sector equality duty assessment completed and signed off before go-live?
Is bias testing repeated after retraining or a change in use, rather than treated as a permanent clearance from the original test?
Is the lawful basis, minimisation rationale, and retention period for training data documented before collection begins?
Is the distinction between data accuracy and statistical accuracy understood and tested separately, rather than treated as one thing?
Are AI-specific security risks, model inversion and membership inference attacks, assessed as part of the system's security review?
Where a supplier is involved, is accountability for each part of the data processing explicitly allocated between the organisation and that supplier?
Are individual rights requests, erasure, restriction, objection, routed through a process that covers the full AI lifecycle, not just the original dataset?
Is a named, trained human overseer assigned to each high-risk system, distinct from the system owner?
Are overseers specifically trained to recognise automation bias, rather than simply given access to the system?
Has the stop or override procedure actually been tested by the people responsible for using it, not just written down?
For biometric identification systems, is the two-person independent verification rule genuinely implemented, not just stated as policy?
Are overseers equipped with an explanation of the system's output suited to their context, rather than a generic technical summary?
Is there a live, documented process for collecting and reviewing safety or performance concerns after deployment, not just a plan for one?
Does the organisation know, before an incident happens, which of the EU AI Act's four serious incident categories would require reporting?
Are the correct external reporting deadlines understood and operationalised, distinct from internal log review timeframes?
For health systems, is there a clear, working separation between the internal safety incident log and external regulatory reporting?
Does a serious incident automatically trigger a reassessment of the system's risk tier, rather than being logged and closed?
Are automatically generated system logs retained for at least six months under a defined process, not on an ad hoc basis?
Is technical documentation retained separately from operational logs, for the full period the law requires, not the same period as the logs?
Can the organisation actually retrieve a specific system's impact assessment, risk tier record, and bias test results on request?
Is access to the audit trail itself secured, given it contains the same sensitive information the underlying systems process?
Has the organisation made a deliberate decision about whether to pursue external certification, rather than never having considered it?
